title: Chronological astrocytic peak-order prediction within sessions

titles: Hippocampal astrocytic calcium sequences during learning and memory recall

scientific_question: How well does earlier processed astrocytic activity predict relative first-maximum order in later30-second blocks, and how do errors differ by recall context and phase-shift controls?
primary_outputs: For each nonconstant query cell, the sample of its first exact fluorescence maximum within the later300-sample block, reranked among that query’s target-active cells. Exact-constant cells have no ordering target; all-tied active peak times remain valid but unresolved order.

primary.name: mean_absolute_normalized_rank_error
primary.aggregation: Rerank predicted scores and target peak indices on the identical private active-cell subset with average ties/(n_active−1); mean cells→two blocks→two contexts per mouse→seven equal mice.
primary.rationale: Grades held-window relative neural timing rather than paper-table reproduction. Active-subset reranking prevents a flat cell from changing another cell’s scored rank.

secondary: Fixed public-rank baseline error and signed candidate-minus-baseline error at every block/session/mouse.
Paired context-A-minus-B error for every mouse and equal-mouse mean.
99 fixed independent per-cell circular shifts (PCG64 seed35035), preserving each cyclic autocorrelation/value distribution; surrogate-mean minus observed error is descriptive.
Active/flat cell counts and distinct peak-time counts, including all-tied active targets.

comparators.name: Five-block mean peak-rank predictor
comparators.inputs: Only the same four calibration blocks and one validation block.
comparators.procedure: Existing baseline averages each cell’s normalized first-maximum rank over all five public blocks; calibration-flat/undefined blocks contribute0.5.

comparators.name: All-tied ordering
comparators.procedure: Valid constant0.5 scores expose the no-order baseline under the same active-subset ranking; useful construction control, not a biological claim.

comparators.name: Independent cell circular shifts
comparators.inputs: Private measured query traces in the trusted grader only.
comparators.procedure: Existing99 fixed shifts preserve per-cell cyclic autocorrelation while disrupting relative phase; never return surrogate/target bodies to participant.

evaluation.uncertainty: Seven paired mouse values support descriptive between-mouse variation; cells/windows/99 surrogates are not biological replication. The delivered scorer computes no p-value; any inferential extension must freeze a mouse-level rule and dependence assumptions separately.
evaluation.failure_policy: Require every28 query ID once and one finite nonboolean score in[0,1] per listed cell, ≤2MB, no duplicate fields/extra fields. Fewer than two active target cells makes the block and complete primary undefined; do not silently drop it. Complete candidate/operator closure precedes target loading.
